# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 for ARM with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support
# This image is pre-configured for multi-node HPC workloads on AWS.
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set environment variable to ensure builds are non-interactive
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies required for LAMMPS
# Includes compilers, cmake, git, networking tools, and fftw library.
# ca-certificates are installed as requested.
# The apt cache is cleaned to keep the image layer small.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a temporary directory for the source code and build process
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code from the official repository
RUN git clone https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git

# Configure, compile, and install LAMMPS
# The build is configured using CMake to leverage MPI for multi-node execution
# It specifically uses the mpicc and mpicxx wrappers from the base image.
# The REAXFF package is enabled as required for the 'lammps-reax' application.
# Common packages KSPACE and MOLECULE are also included.
RUN mkdir -p /build/lammps/build && cd /build/lammps/build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
        -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
        -D PKG_KSPACE=yes \
        -D PKG_MOLECULE=yes && \
    # Compile using all available CPU cores for speed
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system-wide location on the PATH
    cp ./lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final runtime working directory
WORKDIR /workspace

# Copy the example files for the HNS ReaxFF benchmark into the WORKDIR
RUN cp /build/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /workspace/

# Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size
RUN rm -rf /build

# Verify that the 'lmp' executable is correctly installed and available on the PATH
RUN which lmp

# Set a default command to start an interactive shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS experiment
# on an ARM-based AWS E-series CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
# It leverages the Flux Operator to manage a parallel job across multiple nodes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' Kubernetes namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Number of pods (nodes) for the MiniCluster. Set to 4 as required.
  size: 4

  # Total number of MPI tasks. This will run one task per pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Do not delete pods after the job finishes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict mode for logging to catch potential issues.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration section.
  flux:
    # Specify ARM architecture as required for the AWS instance type.
    arch: "arm"
    # This configuration disables the sidecar container for Flux,
    # running Flux binaries within the main application container.
    container:
      disable: true
      # Use the ARM-compatible flux-view image as instructed.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

  # Define the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command will be wrapped by 'flux run' by the operator.
      # This is the LAMMPS command for the reaxff.hns benchmark.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # Ensure containers are not designated as single-purpose launchers.
      launcher: false

      # Always pull the container image to ensure the latest version is used.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # Request AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for high-performance networking.
      # This is required for efficient multi-node communication on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

updates.reason: Previous run was severely under-subscribed, using only 1 task per 64-core node. The new configuration utilizes all 256 cores across 4 nodes and increases the problem size by 64x to match the core count, which is expected to significantly improve the FOM.

The previous run achieved a strong FOM by scaling to the maximum 4 nodes (256 cores). This attempt further increases the problem size by over 3x (from a replication factor of 512 to 1728) to test memory limits and push for a higher total throughput.

The FOM peaked at 1.220 Matom-step/s on 4 nodes with a problem replication of 8x8x8. The subsequent attempt with a larger problem size (12x12x12) failed to produce a result, indicating resource limits (likely memory) were exceeded. The configuration is now considered optimized.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 12 -v y 12 -v z 12 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST parse a result to include the units for katom or Matom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
